expected.rationale: the program loads a class out of this archive on the firing signal, and the archive is not on the class path — so the load itself is what opens the file. This is the condition where an opening of the archive exists to be observed at all

fixture_notes.vulnerable_package_selection: log4j-core 2.14.1, verified against this image with the scanner used here: three findings including CVE-2021-44228 at CRITICAL, attributed to app/log4j-core-2.14.1.jar. Chosen because it is reported at the highest severity, is a library rather than a service, and its archive is named directly by the scan report
fixture_notes.layout: the library is a file of its own, reached through a loader built on the firing signal rather than through the class path
fixture_notes.system_call_level_truth: none; the system-call capture rate is reported as unavailable
fixture_notes.open_condition: load_open: the archive is present but not on the class path, so the runtime does not open it at startup and the load is what opens it. The separate-archives condition is the same load with the file already open
fixture_notes.thread_granularity: none, and the consequence is recorded rather than worked around. This runtime's own thread identifier is unrelated to the operating system's, so the occurrence log names no thread number — and a pairing whose thread condition cannot be checked is counted as undecidable, not as a capture. Both per-occurrence rates for this case are therefore over whatever remains decidable, and are reported alongside the undecidable count rather than as if the whole denominator had been judged
